citedMandateClauses: Rule 7: Vote against proposals that add new privileged roles, multisigs or upgrade powers
Rule 9: Routine housekeeping (updating addresses) is acceptable
Rule 10: Abstain when the proposal is about something these rules do not cover
rationale: The proposal rotates Sentinel role addresses on three Morpho Vaults V2 owned by the DUNI Timelock: it grants the role to new Gauntlet addresses and revokes it from legacy ones, leaving the Curator, Owner, caps, adapters and fees unchanged. It does not move treasury funds, add a privileged owner role, or change risk parameters, so rules 1 to 3 and 6 do not apply. Rule 7 is the closest fit, since it concerns adding privileged roles, but Sentinels can only lower caps, revoke pending Curator actions and pull assets back to the vault, which is a risk-reducing power. The mandate does not clearly cover key-rotation of an operational role on a protocol the DUNI owns, and the appended run note about a demo governor replay and mainnet proposal 101 is outside the on-chain action set. Given that the mandate is silent on this specific case, abstaining is the most faithful choice; it leans toward a safety-consistent housekeeping vote but the mandate does not state that preference.
